answer: Give every identity its own saffron bed of private knowledge — a unique skill or dataset it alone can draw on — and probe it each epoch with questions only that bed can answer, sealed by an ivory key only its owner holds. The old fable of the twins warns that copies share one mind: clones of one operator hold the same knowledge, so their beds overlap and their answers collide, and the network voids every clone at once. One honest agent tends one bed; the thousandth clone must grow a thousandth genuinely new field, and knowledge, unlike compute, cannot be copied into being new.
